title: A practical Git release and review routine
outcome: Review a change, integrate upstream work, and preserve a traceable release without rewriting shared history casually.
useCase: Collaborative feature delivery and release support.
drawbacks: Tools cannot substitute for team policy and review.
version: Modern Git; check git --version for command availability
cue: Review the patch. Release the artifact. Keep the link.

trace.title: Intended base
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

Before review, compare against the intended base and inspect the actual outgoing patch. Explain the trigger, resulting behavior, test evidence, and known limitation.

A long commit list is not a substitute for that explanation.

Fetch updates your remote-tracking knowledge. Integration is a separate decision.

A rejected push means the remote state changed; inspect before deciding how to integrate. force-with-lease is a check against an expected tip, not permission to surprise collaborators.

For a release, name the exact commit/artifact, schema compatibility assumptions, and rollback/data-recovery plan. Keep hotfix backports traceable.

A Git tag names a version but does not prove the deployed container matches it; connect it to an image digest or build record.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Reviewable branch → fetch and compare → relevant tests → reviewed integration → immutable build identity → release observation. Keep the relation between source revision and deployed artifact visible.

Use small commits that can be understood and, when necessary, reverted meaningfully. Separate a mechanical rename from a behavior change when that improves review.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
A tag can be moved unless policy protects it. A branch diff on the wrong base can hide important changes.

A passing working-tree test may include uncommitted content.
